title: A pool run's --max-usd cap counts the runs in flight and its dry run prices the kinds it runs, so a capped run neither passes its cap nor stops short of its rows
goal: benchmarks.py run pool starts no run once the finished runs plus the runs in flight, each at its kind's mean cost, would pass --max-usd; its --dry-run prices each kind at its own mean cost, not the all-kinds mean (SP-kp3boz7z: ST-qm6wuqq4's paid run, 60 runs on sc_absent and sc_partial with --jobs 8, was estimated at 3.51 USD, billed 5.72 USD against a 5 USD cap and stopped 3 runs short)

gates.question: Does the run to start count in the --max-usd check beside the finished runs and the runs in flight, and may the first run of a shape start when its price alone passes its part of the cap?
options: Count only finished and in-flight runs: no run starts once they reach the cap, so the spend can pass it by one run
Count the run to start too, and start the first run of a shape whatever its price while its part of the cap is above 0: no estimated overshoot, and a cap below one run's price still starts one
Count the run to start with no exception: a cap below the first run's price starts none
gates.recommendation: Count the run to start too, and start the first run of a shape whatever its price while its part of the cap is above 0: no estimated overshoot, and a cap below one run's price still starts one
gates.answer: Count the run to start too, and start the first run of a shape whatever its price while its part of the cap is above 0: no estimated overshoot, and a cap below one run's price still starts one

gates.question: Which price does a kind take in the estimate when no earlier record of its arm label holds a cell of that kind?
options: The label's all-kinds cell, then another kb arm's cell of the same kind, its all cell, then the default
Another kb arm's cell of the same kind first, then the label's all-kinds cell, then the default
Refuse the dry run, naming the kind with no price
gates.recommendation: The label's all-kinds cell, then another kb arm's cell of the same kind, its all cell, then the default
gates.answer: The label's all-kinds cell, then another kb arm's cell of the same kind, its all cell, then the default

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 5 of 19, "Benchmark measurement: percentiles, a comparable router arm, a spend cap that holds and a corrected report"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. Premise: bench_pool.run_tasks starts a task while spent_usd() (finished runs only) is under the cap, so up to --jobs runs in flight pass it; and assumed_run prices a label at its all-kinds mean. Run at planning on main: run_tasks over 10 tasks at 1.0 USD each, jobs=4, cap=3.0 started 5 and spent 5.0 (cap passed by 2). Dry run: assumed_run reads the label's all cell only; SP-kp3boz7z billed 5.72 against 3.51 estimated. No paid probe, no spend cap gate: the change moves the cap's start rule and the estimate, no count or billed price of a run; both checks use a fake runner. Docs to correct with it: benchmarks.md (the paragraph on --max-usd says the spend can pass X by up to --jobs runs and prices a label at its all cell's mean), the help of --max-usd, tools.md.
